headline: Discussed Beta Technologies' 101-acre master plan at 3070 Williston Road and closed a 600 Spear Street permit appeal.
summary: The Beta master plan for 101 acres north and south of Williston Road drew staff questions on traffic, civic space, and building size. The applicant agreed to several changes, including a DaVinci Drive traffic signal if three of four warrants are met. After public comment, members closed the application 6-0, and a separate vote closed the 600 Spear Street appeal, where the attorney argued a two-year state deadline applies.
decisions: Closed the appeal of the 600 Spear Street zoning permit expiration; all present voted in favor.
Closed the Beta Technologies master plan application for 3070 Williston Road, 6-0, with no approval recorded in the minutes.
Approved the minutes of 1 and 15 September 2026, 6-0, as written and/or amended.

Mr. Lenski then moved to approve the Minutes of 1 and 15 September 2026 as written and/or amended. Ms. Lesko seconded. Motion passed 6-0.

decision_titles: Appeal of Zoning Permit #24-436 at 600 Spear Street
Beta Technologies master plan, 3070 Williston Road
plain_text:
PAGE 1 
MINUTES 
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 
6 OCTOBER 2026 
 
The South Burlington Development Review Board held a regular meeting on 
Tuesday, 6 October 2026, at 7:00 p.m. in the Auditorium, City Hall, 180 Market 
Street, and via Go to Meeting interactive technology. 
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: Q. Mann, Chair; M. Behr, F. Kochman, J. Lesko, T. Lenski, C. 
Johnston 
 
ALSO PRESENT:  M. Keene, A. Levin, Development Review Planners; P. Conner, 
Director of Planning & Zoning; C. Roy, A. Wood, K. Sentoff, B. Avery, F. 
Vonturkovich, D. Fissette, A. Gagnon, J. Dagesse 
 
1. Instructions on exiting the building in case of an emergency:    
 
Ms. Mann provided instructions on emergency exit from the building. 
 
2. Additions, deletions, or changes in order of agenda items: 
 
No changes were made to the agenda. 
 
3. Comments and questions from the public not related to the Agenda: 
 
No issues were raised. 
 
4. Announcements: 
 
There were no announcements. 
 
5. Reconsideration of APZ-APPEAL-2026-2 of Frank VonTurkevich appeal 
the decision of the Administrative Officer that Zoning Permit #24-436 
has expired, 600 Spear Street:
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 6 October 2026 PAGE 2 
 
Ms. Keene stepped down as it is her decision in her role as the Administrative 
Officer that is being appealed.  Mr. Conner joined the Board for this item. 
 
Ms. Mann reviewed the history and said the Board is most interested in the 
State’s 2-year regulation.  She then swore in those who might testify. 
 
Mr. Roy, attorney for the 600 Spear Street entities, presented two main points as 
follows: 
 
a. It is the appellant’s belief that within a one-year deadline, there 
was more than enough activity to meet the standard of “good 
faith intent.”  His client spent over $20,000 for site prep and more.  
The project would have continued had it not been for the issues 
that arose. 
 
b. It is clear that the one-year deadline is no longer valid.  It was a 
PUD approval that gave rise to the zoning permit.  State Statute 
says a 2-year deadline applies. 
 
Mr. Roy said his client looks forward to proceeding with the project and providing 
much needed housing. 
 
Ms. Mann asked for public comment.  There were no public comments. 
 
Ms. Lesko moved to close PZ-APPEAL-2026-2.  Mr. Behr seconded.  The motion 
passed with all present voting in favor. 
  
6. Continued Master Plan Application #PZ-MASTER-2026-2 of Beta 
Technologies, Inc., to establish a Master Plan for a 101-acre area 
consisting of 3 development areas including the previously approved 
Beta Master Plan area plus newly acquired properties in immediate 
proximity to the north and south of Williston Road, 3070 Williston Road: 
 
Mr. Gendron noted that they have made updates based on feedback from the 
DRB, staff and neighbors.  He added that they had not previously done a good job 
to indicate this is a Beta/BTV plan.  He stressed that this is BTV land.  They have 
also revised a lot of the language to recognize that all development will require
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 6 October 2026 PAGE 3 
discussion with a number of agencies.  This is a shared effort with many 
stakeholders. 
 
Staff comments were then addressed as follows: 
 
 #1. Staff notes that for the DRB to approve the Master Plan, they feel the 
applicant must at least commit to a suite of potential mitigation measures for the 
proposed impacts of the Master Plan.  Staff recommended the Board ask the 
applicant to explain the rationale behind added/changed language and, based on 
that explanation, recommends the DRB consider whether to require the applicant 
to revise the language of the application narrative and IIP to reflect a higher 
degree of commitment to improvements enumerated therein as they will be 
incorporated into the Findings.  This involves BTV being a co-applicant to the 
Plan. 
 
Mr. Gendron said they agree to this. 
 
 #2. Regarding the neighborhood meeting, staff asked whether there were 
any updates based on the second meeting.  Mr. Gendron said they received more 
comments mostly related to traffic.  These have been incorporated into the Master 
Plan. 
 
 #3. Staff recommends the DRB consider whether to require the applicant to 
make minor modification to the proposed parameters for Development Area 1.  
Ms. Keene noted there is not the same level of detail as there is for those in 
Development Areas 2 and 3.  Mr. Gendron said the goal is to have people walk 
into a nice building.  Ms. Mann suggested the applicant revisit the “entrance 
section.”  Mr. Behr agreed.  He said the buildings the DRB has reviewed so far 
have been fine. It would be nice to have more detail here. 
 
 #4. Regarding civic spaces, Ms. Keene reminded the applicant that for every 
1,000 sq. ft., they will need 1/10 of an acre of civic space.  If they build only half of 
a building, they would never get to the civic space requirements.  She suggested a 
mid-point recalibration.  Ms. Mann noted that what the DRB had landed on was 
that a CO for a building would not be issued until there is a CO for the civic space.  
Mr. Kochman stressed that the requirement is for 10% of an area to be civic space.  
Ms. Mann added that the DRB would want the civic space to be near the building.  
Mr. Kochman suggested a stipulation that at the end of a development project 
there will be 10% civic space; if Beta touches a development area, there must be 
10% civic space by the end of the Master Plan.  The applicant was OK with this
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 6 October 2026 PAGE 4 
stipulation.    Mr. Behr clarified that if the applicant pulls a permit for an area, 
before that permit is closed out, the civic space must be built. 
 
 #5. Staff raised the question of having civic space for one area being built in 
another area.  Mr. Gendron showed where this could happen.  Ms. Mann said the 
DRB could say “no,” but they would entertain a proposal at a future site plan 
review. 
 
 #6. Staff questioned the proposed 14% traffic impact by using CATMA.  Ms. 
Mann reminded the applicant that they can use only up to 10%.  Mr. Gagnon said 
they are already there with bus passes, incentives to car pool, etc.  They thought 
they would just put it all under CATMA.  Ms. Keene suggested counting what gets 
you to 10% under CATMA and then doing “other things.”  Mr. Gagnon noted 
there is a transit stop right out front.  Their goal is to be over 14%. 
 
 #7. The applicant was asked to clarify verbally and in writing whether the 
proposal for every 75 external trips or for every 75 trips specific to the use 
regardless of internal capture.  Mr. Gagnon said it is based on external trips.  They 
will update the IIP to indicate that. 
 
 #8. Regarding updates based on DPW comments, Mr. Gendron said they 
are OK with all of them. 
 
 #9. Regarding comments from Planning & Zoning, Mr. Gendron said they 
are OK with all of them. 
 
 #10. Staff recommends the DRB require a specific trigger for a traffic signal 
at DaVinci Drive.  Mr. Gendron said they are OK with providing a signal if only 3 of 
the 4 warrants are met.  They will also provide the number of trips needed to meet 
the 4th warrant.  VTrans is OK with them putting in the signal before that. 
 
 #11. Staff asked the applicant how they will respond if there is less traffic 
than the model indicates.  Staff suggests the applicant update the forecast with 
each implementation.  Mr. Gagnon said the goal is to follow the City’s priorities 
and do 1-4 first and then re-evaluate at each application.  Ms. Keene said the City 
has a congestion tolerance limit depending on the size of the road and what is the 
acceptable level of service.  If a plan exceeds these, it would be an automatic 
denial by the DRB.  Mr. Kochman suggested adding the words “and in compliance 
with the relevant standards.”  Members agreed.
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 6 October 2026 PAGE 5 
 #12. Staff asked for a specific trigger for the dedication of Green Tree Drive.  
Mr. Gendron said they would agree to that and come in with a “principal building 
plan in Development Area 3.” 
 
 #13. Regarding buildings shown along Green Tree Drive, staff felt this was a 
mistake and suggested the DRB ask the applicant whether these buildings should 
be shown on DaVinci Drive.  Mr. Gagnon said they will update this to be specific 
to every road. 
 
 #14. Regarding the scale of development, staff recommended the Board 
require a specific maximum footprint  and height of buildings with a specific 
distance from the boundary of the Master Plan.  Mr. Gagnon said there would be a 
15 foot landscape buffer and no building within 65 feet of a residential district.  
They are calculating building height as a median between 2 districts.  Lot 
coverages are 35/60.  Ms. Keene said staff came up with the same figures and 
showed a plan of what those numbers would look like.  Ms. Mann asked what kind 
of commercial activity would occur in the transition area.  Mr. Gendron said they 
didn’t see anything allowed in the IC District that they would exclude.  They would 
exclude loading areas on the residential side of the primary building.  They do not 
anticipate major trucking use. 
 
 #15. Staff asked that the Board clarify with the applicant why they removed 
the Green Tree Drive connection from being “proposed” to being “conceptual.”  
Staff assumes this connection to be an assumed component of the Board’s initial 
acceptance of the circulation and access for the proposed Master Plan.  Mr. 
Gendron said they will clean that up. 
 
 #16. Staff recommends the Board discuss comments of the Fire Marshall 
regarding an additional fire access.  Mr. Gagnon said they are aware of this and 
are already coordinating with the Fire Marshall.  They have worked out a 
temporary wishbone system so the Fire Department gets what it needs.  Ms. 
Mann said this needs to be shown on the materials.  Mr. Gendron said this will be 
a service road, not a public road.  They will label it accordingly.    Ms. Keene noted 
comments from the Water Department regarding increasing the line to 12 inches.  
Mr. Gagnon said they don’t intend to tap in there. 
 
 #17. Regarding updated values for the buildable area table, staff said there 
is no information as to why the numbers changed.  Mr. Gagnon said they got 
information regarding a piece of land that is also not buildable.
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 6 October 2026 PAGE 6 
 #18. Staff recommends the DRB discuss whether the applicant’s proposal 
provides adequate evaluation of wastewater capacity as part of future applications 
under the Master Plan.  Mr. Gendron said they know they can’t do a development 
without upgrading the pump station.  He felt there should be some cost sharing 
on that.  Ms. Keene said that is the City Council’s purview, not the DRB’s. 
 
 #19. Staff asked the applicant to describe how they propose to handle 
stormwater.  Mr. Gendron said there will always be enough stormwater treatment 
area.  They can’t pinpoint now exactly where it can go.  Mr. Behr said it would be 
good for the applicant to describe the techniques they can use for stormwater, 
what tools they might use (e.g., a rain garden).  He did not want to see 110,000 
square feet of retention ponds.  Mr. Gendron said they could shrink the lot 
coverage, if needed.  He stressed that the pie charts shown are the worst case 
scenarios.  Ms. Mann suggested the applicant show the Board something less 
conservative.   
 
 #20. Regarding management of capital assets, staff said the applicant must 
retain responsibility for the infrastructure.  Mr. Kochman suggested language 
such as “Beta will do what they need to do to comply with the Master Plan.”  He 
was not sure how this works for property the Airport already owns.  Staff felt the 
plan was insufficiently specific to ensure future compliance with conditions of the 
Master Plan, specifically the commitment for evaluation and necessary upgrades 
to infrastructure capacity on a project by project basis.  Mr. Kochman suggested 
the Board deliberate before closing the application and to give the applicant a 
“decision.”  He felt this is big enough that the Board shouldn’t force the applicant 
into something.  Ms. Mann suggested a draft decision which the applicant could 
come back to discuss.   
 
Mr. Gendron said they were ready to close tonight as they have a first application 
that is ready to go.  Mr. Behr cited the risk but noted he hadn’t heard anything that 
was really contentious, just some “grey areas.”  Mr. Gendron said nothing there is 
nothing they have heard that they couldn’t live with. 
 
Public comment was then solicited and received as follows: 
 
Ms. Fissette:  Asked how civic space related to non-buildable space.  She was 
specifically concerned with Area 3 and suggested the Board extend the area to 
protect residents.  She noted that Technology Park is now almost exclusively Beta, 
and Beta owns 4 of the homes on her street.  They have houses turning over 
every 6 months.  She said the DRB can guide to applicant in order to protect other
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 6 October 2026 PAGE 7 
citizens.  She felt Beta has already chased small businesses out of the area.  She 
questioned what would happen if Beta fails and noted they have already moved 
some things to South Carolina.  Ms. Mann said what is build will be there whether 
Beta is there or not.  Mr. Gagnon acknowledged that Beta owns 5 of the 20 houses 
on Ms. Fissette’s street.  Mr. Gendron said this gives employees a place to stay 
when they come to Vermont and are not yet settled. 
 
Ms. Lesko then moved to close PZ-MASTER-2026-2.  Mr. Johnston seconded.  
Motion passed 6-0. 
 
7.  Minutes of 1 and 15 September 2026: 
 
The following amendments were made to the Minutes:  On p. 2, the motion 
should pass 5-0 as Mr. Kochman was recused.  P. 12, Item 21 seems unclear, and 
the following language was suggested: There should be a CO for the civic space 
prior to the CO for the building. 
 
Mr. Lenski then moved to approve the Minutes of 1 and 15 September 2026 as 
written and/or amended.  Ms. Lesko seconded.  Motion passed 6-0.  
 
8. Other Business: 
 
No other business was presented. 
 
 
As there was no further business to come before the Board, the meeting was 
adjourned by common consent at 9:21 p.m. 
 
 
 
These minutes were approved by common consent on November 3, 2026
